question:
Each side of the large square in the figure is trisected (divided into three equal parts). The corners of an inscribed square are at these trisection points, as shown. The ratio of the area of the inscribed square to the area of the large square is

[Figure 1](figures/1997_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The regions outside the inscribed square are four right triangles, whose areas are easier to find than the inscribed square's side length. Use one trisection segment as the unit of length. The large square then has side length \(3\) and area \(9\) square units.

At each corner, the two perpendicular legs of the outside triangle have lengths \(1\) and \(2\), as determined by the selected trisection points. Thus each triangle has area
\[
\frac{1\cdot2}{2}=1.
\]
These four triangles and the inscribed square fill the large square without overlapping interiors. The inscribed square therefore has area \(9-4\cdot1=5\). Using the same area unit for both squares, the requested ratio is \(\boxed{\frac{5}{9}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
